automotive-ev-battery.title: Porsche to form EU CO₂ pool with Xpeng
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Porsche has departed Volkswagen Group's EU CO₂ emissions pool to form a regulatory partnership with Chinese EV manufacturer Xpeng beginning in 2026. The arrangement is expected to generate valuable emissions credits for Xpeng as it expands its European vehicle sales.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Kia EV3 starts at under $30,000 in the US
automotive-ev-battery.summary: The Kia EV3 has launched in the United States with starting prices of $29,890 before destination charges, offering up to 321 miles of EPA-estimated range. The compact electric SUV comes standard with a NACS charging port, addressing consumer demand for affordable EV options.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Early switch to EVs delivers significant climate benefits
automotive-ev-battery.summary: A comprehensive US study demonstrates that switching from a functional combustion-engine vehicle to an electric car reduces emissions in 92 percent of modeled scenarios. The research challenges the conventional wisdom that retaining older internal combustion vehicles is more environmentally sustainable.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Waymo Imports 3,200 Zeekr Robotaxis Despite Super High Tariffs
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Waymo has imported 3,200 Zeekr-based Ojai electric robotaxis into the United States despite facing 102.5 percent tariffs on Chinese-produced EVs. The vehicles, which were custom-designed for Waymo's autonomous robotaxi service over several years, represent a significant commitment to autonomous transportation technology.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Togg integrates Electroverse into its Trumore app
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Turkish automaker Togg has integrated the Octopus Electroverse charging platform into its Trumore app, initially providing access to over 220,000 public charging points in Germany. The integration will expand to include access to the Europe-wide Electroverse network of more than 1.4 million charging points.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Honda reportedly taps Tata Technologies for multi-energy platform
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Honda has commissioned Tata Technologies to develop a new vehicle platform capable of supporting multiple powertrains. The flexible platform architecture will enable Honda to adapt quickly to evolving market conditions and regulatory requirements across different regions.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Xing Mobility introduces immersion-cooled batteries for ships
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Xing Mobility has launched two immersion-cooled battery systems specifically engineered for maritime applications. The modular Immersio XM25 solution offers adaptability for various ship types, while the Immersio CTP features cell-to-pack architecture designed for maximum energy density in a compact footprint.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Tesla recalls 20,000 EVs over headlight glare
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Tesla is recalling 20,349 Model 3 and Model Y vehicles in the United States due to low-beam headlights that exceed permitted luminous intensity levels in certain areas. The NHTSA rejected Tesla's petition to avoid the recall, forcing the company to proceed with the safety remediation.

automotive-ev-battery.title: New Zealand offers $21 million in loans for EV chargers
automotive-ev-battery.summary: New Zealand has launched a second funding round for public EV charging infrastructure, allocating approximately NZ$21 million in zero-interest loans to support its goal of 10,000 charge points by 2030. The loans will cover up to half of eligible project costs for qualifying installations.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Scaling Autonomous Freight: Inside Pony.ai's Robotruck Business
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Pony.ai is advancing its autonomous freight operations through development of both heavy-duty Gen-4 trucks and L4-capable urban delivery vehicles. The company's strategy combines shared autonomous technology, automotive-grade production practices, and industry partnerships to scale its robotruck business.

tech-ai.title: As AI safety concerns mount, three pioneers make the case for staying open
tech-ai.summary: Geoffrey Hinton, Fei-Fei Li, and Andrew Ng debated critical issues around AI regulation, open source access, and U.S. competitive positioning against China at the Ai4 conference. The discussion highlights diverging perspectives among leading AI experts on how to balance safety concerns with innovation and openness.

tech-ai.title: AI coding startup Cognition reportedly already in talks to raise at $40B valuation
tech-ai.summary: Cognition, the AI coding assistant startup, is reportedly seeking to raise additional funding at a $40 billion valuation just months after its $1 billion Series B round at $26 billion. The rapid revaluation reflects investor enthusiasm for AI-powered developer tools and the competitive landscape for generative AI startups.

tech-ai.title: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings raises $2B to bring AI to the enterprise
tech-ai.summary: Thrive Holdings has secured $2 billion in Series B funding at a $12 billion valuation from major investors including SoftBank and D1 Capital Partners to expand its enterprise AI offerings. The funding round underscores continued investor confidence in AI solutions targeting business customers.

tech-ai.title: Amazon will train on Twitch streamers' content by default, unless they opt out
tech-ai.summary: Amazon announced that Twitch streamers' content will be used to train its generative AI models by default, with Twitch's Chief Product Officer acknowledging that an opt-in approach would receive minimal participation. The policy shift raises concerns about content creator rights and AI training data practices.

tech-ai.title: Some Claude users are mad that Anthropic's new watermarks will catch them using it at their jobs, classes
tech-ai.summary: Anthropic's new watermarking system for Claude AI output has triggered backlash from users on social media who are concerned about detection in workplace and educational settings. The watermarking technology represents a shift toward transparency but raises questions about AI use policies in professional and academic contexts.

tech-ai.title: How Google's new Pixel 11 phones compare to last year's models
tech-ai.summary: Google announced four new Pixel 11 models featuring the new Tensor G6 chip, improved cameras, and new AI photography tools including Magic Capture and enhanced Gemini Intelligence. The phones represent incremental upgrades with slightly higher pricing than their predecessors.

tech-ai.title: Google's Pixel 11 phone preorders come with up to $350 in gift cards
tech-ai.summary: Google officially launched its Pixel 11 lineup with base pricing starting at $899 for the standard model and up to $1,899 for the Pro Fold variant, offering promotional gift cards valued up to $350 for early adopters. The preorder campaign includes multiple watch size options starting at $399.

tech-ai.title: AI nuclear power firm Fermi finally has a new CEO
tech-ai.summary: Fermi, an AI-focused nuclear power company, appointed Lee McIntire, an independent board member, as CEO more than three months after firing co-founder Toby Neugebauer from the leadership position. The leadership transition marks a significant shift for the company as it develops advanced reactor technology.

tech-ai.title: Twitch streamers can now opt out from training Amazon's AI
tech-ai.summary: Twitch has implemented an opt-out mechanism allowing streamers to prevent their content—including streams, VODs, clips, and chat—from being used to train Amazon's generative AI models. Other AI-supported features such as captions and safety tools remain functional for users who decline generative AI training participation.

tech-ai.title: Northrop's robot space mechanic is a new way to keep satellites at work longer
tech-ai.summary: Northrop Grumman's Mission Robotic Vehicle is making its first attempt to install a new thruster on an aging satellite, demonstrating robotic servicing technology to extend satellite operational lifespans. The mission represents progress in on-orbit satellite maintenance and logistics capabilities.

science-space.title: Farthest 'black hole star' ever found could help solve the James Webb Space Telescope's little red dot mystery
science-space.summary: Astronomers have discovered the most distant black hole star to date, providing crucial evidence that could explain the mysterious "little red dots" observed by the James Webb Space Telescope in the early universe. This finding offers significant insights into the nature and formation of black holes shortly after the Big Bang.

science-space.title: Radiation-shielding vest aced Artemis I lunar test, could protect astronauts on moon and Mars missions
science-space.summary: A radiation-shielding vest successfully completed testing during the Artemis I lunar mission in 2022, demonstrating its potential to protect astronauts during long-duration missions to the Moon and Mars. The vest's successful performance represents a significant advancement in human spaceflight safety technology.

science-space.title: NASA Data Helps Commercial Space Plan Living Off Our Moon
science-space.summary: NASA is providing critical data to commercial companies, including Lunar Station Corp., to support plans for extracting and processing lunar resources such as water, iron, and titanium. The precise mapping of resource locations will determine optimal landing sites and mining operations for sustainable lunar habitation.

science-space.title: NASA Upgrades Vertical Motion Simulator for Modern Mission Needs
science-space.summary: NASA has upgraded its Vertical Motion Simulator, the world's largest of its kind, to better prepare astronauts and pilots for next-generation spacecraft, air taxi, and lunar landing operations. The enhanced simulator leverages modern technology to provide more realistic training scenarios for current and future space missions.

science-space.title: Total solar eclipse 2026 thrills millions with a stunning cosmic spectacle
science-space.summary: A total solar eclipse on August 12, 2026, captivated millions of skywatchers as it crossed Greenland, Iceland, and Spain, producing spectacular photographs and video documentation of the celestial event. The eclipse provided unprecedented viewing opportunities across multiple Northern Hemisphere locations.

science-space.title: What Is the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope?
science-space.summary: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope represents NASA's newest astrophysics observatory, designed to survey expansive sections of space and investigate fundamental cosmic mysteries including dark energy, dark matter, and exoplanets. This advanced instrument will significantly enhance our understanding of the universe's composition and structure.

science-space.title: NASA Astronaut Mike Fincke Leaves NASA, Career Includes 4 Spaceflights
science-space.summary: NASA astronaut Mike Fincke has concluded his 30-year career with the agency, during which he completed four spaceflights, spent 549 days in space, and conducted nine spacewalks in support of International Space Station operations. Fincke's departure marks the end of a distinguished career that shaped multiple chapters of NASA's human spaceflight history.

science-space.title: SpaceX wraps Starlink double header day with the launch of 24 Starlink satellites from California
science-space.summary: SpaceX successfully launched 24 additional Starlink internet satellites to orbit from California on August 11, 2026, concluding a productive dual-launch day for the company. The ongoing deployment continues SpaceX's expansion of its global internet satellite constellation.

science-space.title: Perseid meteor shower peaks under perfect skies tonight
science-space.summary: The Perseid meteor shower reached its annual peak under favorable viewing conditions, offering skywatchers an optimal opportunity to observe this prolific celestial event. The article provides guidance on timing, location, and viewing methods for maximizing observation of the meteor shower.

science-space.title: Quality Assessment Report Evaluates Polar Geospatial Center EarthDEM Elevation Products
science-space.summary: A comprehensive quality assessment report evaluates commercial Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) provided by the Polar Geospatial Center's EarthDEM products. The assessment provides the scientific community with critical information regarding the reliability and accuracy of these geospatial data resources.

world-news.title: Major Russian grain export terminals hit in Ukraine Black Sea port attack
world-news.summary: Grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine are significantly declining as the two nations conduct reciprocal attacks on each other's shipping facilities and ports in the Black Sea. The disruption to global grain supplies carries major implications for international food security and commodity markets.

world-news.title: Iran war live: US, Tehran exchange opposing claims over Hormuz control
world-news.summary: The United States and Iran are engaged in an escalating dispute over control of the strategic Strait of Hormuz, with President Trump claiming total US control while Tehran insists the US must accede to Iranian demands. The standoff over one of the world's most critical shipping chokepoints has significant implications for global energy markets and international stability.

world-news.title: US strikes in Yemen killed 153 civilians in 2025, says Pentagon review
world-news.summary: A declassified Pentagon review reveals that United States military strikes against Yemen's Houthis resulted in at least 153 civilian deaths during 2025, raising international concerns about civilian harm in the campaign. The disclosure occurs amid broader scrutiny of US military operations in the region and their impact on non-combatants.

world-news.title: Israeli settlers besieging Palestinian families in West Bank village
world-news.summary: Israeli security forces have withdrawn from a West Bank village where approximately a dozen settlers have maintained a siege against two Palestinian families since Sunday. The incident reflects escalating tensions between Israeli settlers and Palestinian residents in occupied territories.

world-news.title: Thousands of Canadians call for US ambassador's expulsion
world-news.summary: An online petition accusing US Ambassador Pete Hoekstra of diplomatic interference in Canadian domestic affairs has garnered more than 60,000 signatures from Canadian citizens. The controversy reflects growing tensions in US-Canada relations and questions about appropriate diplomatic conduct.

world-news.title: Hegseth cautions that ICC may investigate US boat strikes in Latin America
world-news.summary: US Defence Secretary Hegseth acknowledged that the International Criminal Court may investigate American military boat strikes conducted in Latin America while vowing to continue the campaign against drug cartels. The statement highlights potential friction between US military operations and international legal oversight, while noting Colombia has joined a regional military coalition.

world-news.title: Morocco says working to prevent potential new Ceuta crossings surge
world-news.summary: Morocco's Interior Ministry has announced increased security measures along its borders with the Spanish exclaves of Ceuta and Melilla to prevent a potential surge in migrant crossings. The move reflects ongoing tensions over migration routes and border security in the Mediterranean region.

world-news.title: Members of Trump's cabinet remained on decoy plane, after president's quiet exit
world-news.summary: President Trump discreetly departed from a NATO summit in Turkey by boarding a separate aircraft due to security concerns involving Iran, leaving cabinet members aboard a decoy plane. The incident underscores elevated security threats facing US leadership at international diplomatic gatherings.

world-news.title: Thousands missing after Colombia quake as rescue continues
world-news.summary: A significant earthquake in Colombia has left thousands missing as rescue and recovery operations continue in affected areas. The disaster has prompted international humanitarian response and assistance.

world-news.title: At least 44 die as ferry sinks in Zimbabwe's Lake Kariba
world-news.summary: A passenger ferry capsized and sank in Zimbabwe's Lake Kariba after being struck by strong waves, resulting in at least 44 deaths. The maritime disaster raises questions about vessel safety standards and emergency response procedures in the region.

finance-markets.title: US inflation falls to 3.4% in July
finance-markets.summary: US inflation declined to 3.4% in July, easing pressure on the Federal Reserve to maintain elevated interest rates and potentially clearing the path for future rate cuts. The decline occurred despite ongoing geopolitical tensions, as petrol prices moderated from earlier peaks.

finance-markets.title: Wall Street giants bet Nvidia's AI chips will defy the laws of finance
finance-markets.summary: Major private capital firms are making substantial wagers that Nvidia's semiconductor chips will maintain their value over extended periods, betting against traditional depreciation patterns in the hardware market. This reflects confidence in sustained artificial intelligence demand and Nvidia's market dominance.

finance-markets.title: Asian Stocks Rise as Rate Hike Bets Ease, Oil Dips: Markets Wrap
finance-markets.summary: Asian equity markets rallied following softer-than-expected US inflation data that reduced expectations for near-term Federal Reserve rate increases, while crude oil prices pulled back from their six-session winning streak. The market reaction reflects improved sentiment regarding the global monetary policy outlook.

finance-markets.title: Korean Stocks Rise 22% in 10 Days as Chip Rally Regains Steam
finance-markets.summary: South Korea's benchmark stock index surged 22% over ten days, positioning itself to enter a technical bull market as global semiconductor stocks rebounded sharply following a challenging previous month. The rally reflects renewed investor appetite for artificial intelligence-related equities.

finance-markets.title: How a bad trade pushed a US mortgage giant into a $2bn lifeline
finance-markets.summary: Arizona-based mortgage lender UWM Holdings secured a $2 billion rescue package from Oaktree Capital following losses on an ill-fated hedging trade, with billionaire Mat Ishbia facilitating the last-minute deal. The situation underscores continued stress in the US residential mortgage sector amid elevated interest rates.

finance-markets.title: Japan's Producer Price Gains Stay High as BOJ Mulls Rate Path
finance-markets.summary: Japan's producer price inflation remained elevated in July, maintaining cost pressures on corporations as the Bank of Japan deliberates on whether to implement additional interest rate increases to combat inflation. The persistent price growth complicates the central bank's monetary policy decisions.

finance-markets.title: Brazil Backs Spending Control Measure in Fiscal Nod From Lula
finance-markets.summary: Brazil's Congress approved fiscal spending measures designed to demonstrate budgetary discipline under President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, signaling commitment to economic restraint ahead of the upcoming presidential election. The approval aims to restore investor confidence in Brazil's macroeconomic management.

finance-markets.title: Poorer Americans are struggling to make 'ends meet', top Fed official says
finance-markets.summary: Boston Federal Reserve branch head Susan Collins warned that lower-income Americans face significant financial hardship, while signaling support for a September interest rate increase if inflation remains elevated. The comments highlight the distributional impacts of monetary tightening on vulnerable populations.

finance-markets.title: Mark Walter's insurers rush to unwind affiliated investments
finance-markets.summary: Billionaire Mark Walter's insurance company TWG Global is executing a rapid unwinding of affiliated investments and restructuring operations as prosecutors investigate the group's financial practices. The firm is simultaneously seeking refinancing and outside capital injection amid regulatory scrutiny.

finance-markets.title: Rio Tinto Australia Aluminum Plant Gets $1.8 Billion Bailout
finance-markets.summary: Rio Tinto and consortium partners secured a A$2.5 billion Australian government bailout for the nation's largest aluminum smelter to address mounting operational costs driven by elevated energy prices. The rescue package demonstrates government intervention to preserve critical industrial capacity.

health-biotech.title: WHO says Trump's latest vaccine policy order is misguided
health-biotech.summary: The World Health Organization has criticized the White House's executive order to overhaul the vaccine schedule, warning that the changes could subject children to more needles and increased disease risk. Global health leaders have expressed concern about the policy's potential impact on childhood immunization programs.

health-biotech.title: Talks on launch of clinical trial of Ebola vaccine in DRC advance, WHO says
health-biotech.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo and the World Health Organization are advancing discussions to expedite the start of a multi-armed Phase 3 clinical trial for Ebola vaccines. This development represents progress in efforts to evaluate vaccine candidates in the region most affected by the disease.

health-biotech.title: Four questions on new safety warnings for Neurocrine's Vykat XR
health-biotech.summary: Experts on Prader-Willi syndrome have raised safety concerns regarding Neurocrine Biosciences' medicine Vykat XR, with the treatment potentially linked to seven deaths. The warnings highlight serious adverse events that warrant immediate clinical and regulatory attention.

health-biotech.title: Cancer patients face longer wait times to begin treatment, according to new study
health-biotech.summary: A new study reveals that cancer patients are experiencing extended delays in beginning treatment compared to a decade ago, with longer wait times documented across all cancer types examined. The findings suggest systemic challenges in cancer care delivery and treatment initiation.

health-biotech.title: Definium Therapeutics says its LSD therapy eased anxiety in late-stage trial
health-biotech.summary: Definium Therapeutics reported that its oral LSD candidate significantly improved symptoms in patients with generalized anxiety disorder in the first of two Phase 3 clinical trials. The positive results represent an important milestone for the investigational psychedelic-based therapeutic approach.

health-biotech.title: Eli Lilly files first lawsuits over retatrutide 'black market'
health-biotech.summary: Eli Lilly has initiated litigation against six U.S. companies accused of illegally selling black-market versions of its investigational obesity and diabetes drug retatrutide, which remains in clinical trials. The lawsuits represent the pharmaceutical company's first legal action addressing unauthorized distribution of the experimental medication.

health-biotech.title: Vaccine makers throw cold water on separating MMR vaccine
health-biotech.summary: Vaccine manufacturers and clinical development experts have expressed skepticism about the feasibility of separating the combined measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine into individual shots, as recently ordered by President Trump. Industry analysts argue that while theoretically possible, the practical implementation would be challenging and costly.

health-biotech.title: Trump administration's new 'treatment first' addiction toolkit emphasizes faith, abstinence
health-biotech.summary: The White House has unveiled a new addiction treatment toolkit that prioritizes faith-based and abstinence-focused approaches while de-emphasizing other harm reduction strategies. The policy acknowledges the use of addiction medications but signals a shift away from comprehensive harm reduction frameworks.

health-biotech.title: AbCellera, Silence and InduPro all raise significant funding
health-biotech.summary: AbCellera, a Vancouver-based biotech company, has completed a $200 million equity offering following positive Phase 2 trial results in hot flashes treatment, with Silence Therapeutics and InduPro also securing substantial funding rounds. The capital raises reflect investor confidence in these biotechnology firms' pipeline progress.

health-biotech.title: Opinion: The Lindsay Clancy case shows the limits of postpartum psychiatry
health-biotech.summary: Experts have highlighted gaps in the understanding and treatment of postpartum psychiatric illnesses, using the Lindsay Clancy case to illustrate systemic deficiencies in perinatal mental health care. The commentary underscores the need for improved clinical approaches and better support systems for affected patients.

crypto-web3.title: Goldman Sachs leaps into bitcoin income ETFs with $2.25 billion NEOS buyout
crypto-web3.summary: Goldman Sachs has acquired NEOS Investments for $2.25 billion to expand its bitcoin and ethereum income ETF offerings, bringing its total ETF assets under management to $130 billion. The deal represents a significant institutional push into crypto derivatives and directly competes with BlackRock's BITA bitcoin ETF offering.

crypto-web3.title: New York City Council opens probe into prediction market platforms
crypto-web3.summary: The New York City Council has initiated an investigation into prediction market platforms over concerns regarding alleged false, deceptive, or abusive marketing tactics. This regulatory scrutiny signals increasing governmental attention to the prediction market sector's compliance practices.

crypto-web3.title: Prediction markets should dial back faulty filings for incentives to boost trading: CFTC
crypto-web3.summary: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission has warned prediction market platforms such as Kalshi and Polymarket to improve their compliance practices, citing concerns that faulty incentive filings could enable market manipulation. The regulatory guidance suggests the industry is developing problematic compliance habits that require correction.

crypto-web3.title: SEC clears Franklin Templeton funds to use onchain BENJI system for cash management
crypto-web3.summary: The Securities and Exchange Commission issued a no-action letter to Franklin Templeton permitting its registered funds to utilize its BENJI/FOBXX onchain system for institutional cash management. This approval represents a significant regulatory endorsement of blockchain-based treasury management for traditional financial institutions.

crypto-web3.title: Standard Chartered-led Anchorpoint launches Hong Kong dollar stablecoin
crypto-web3.summary: Standard Chartered has led the launch of HKDAP, a Hong Kong dollar-backed stablecoin through Anchorpoint, with HashKey Exchange and OSL Group authorized as institutional distributors. The stablecoin enables professional and institutional investors to mint and redeem tokens, expanding regulated digital currency infrastructure in Asia.

crypto-web3.title: Securitize falls 20% after earnings miss as tokenization revenue falls short
crypto-web3.summary: Securitize's stock declined 20 percent following its first earnings report since going public, as tokenization revenue underperformed expectations despite record tokenized assets and elevated trading activity. The earnings miss signals potential challenges in converting growing transaction volumes into proportional revenue growth.

crypto-web3.title: Miden bets on privacy stablecoins with introduction of USDCx
crypto-web3.summary: Miden has introduced USDCx, a privacy-focused stablecoin enabling users to conduct transactions while concealing balances, counterparties, and transaction histories, while maintaining selective disclosure capabilities for regulatory compliance. The product addresses growing demand for confidential financial transactions within regulated frameworks.

crypto-web3.title: Polymarket taps ex-Uber and Bird exec Travis VanderZanden to boost growth
crypto-web3.summary: Polymarket has appointed Travis VanderZanden, a veteran of Uber, Lyft, and Bird known for growth acceleration strategies, as chief growth officer. The hire signals Polymarket's intent to scale operations amid increasing regulatory scrutiny and competitive pressure in the prediction market sector.

crypto-web3.title: Ethereum staking climbs to 34% as proposal targets validator rewards and ETH treasury firm yields
crypto-web3.summary: Ethereum's staking ratio has reached 34 percent of total supply, with researchers proposing EIP-8361, a tapered issuance burn mechanism that would increase token destruction as staking participation rises. The proposal aims to manage validator economics and network treasury yields as staking adoption continues to expand.

crypto-web3.title: Wintermute plans $1 billion AI push beyond crypto: Bloomberg
crypto-web3.summary: Wintermute is pursuing a one-billion-dollar expansion into artificial intelligence and non-crypto markets with the goal of deriving over 50 percent of revenues from outside the crypto sector by 2027, up from 10 percent currently. The strategic pivot reflects broader industry diversification efforts amid evolving regulatory conditions.

startups-vc.title: AI coding startup Cognition reportedly already in talks to raise at $40B valuation
startups-vc.summary: Cognition, an AI coding startup, is reportedly in early-stage discussions to raise funding at a $40 billion valuation, representing a significant increase from its $26 billion valuation just months earlier when it raised $1 billion. The potential mega-round underscores investor enthusiasm for AI-powered developer tools in an increasingly competitive market.

startups-vc.title: Lovable confirms new $13.3B valuation, raises another $400M
startups-vc.summary: Lovable, an AI development platform, has confirmed a $13.3 billion valuation while raising an additional $400 million in funding. The company has achieved $500 million in annualized run rate revenue as of June, demonstrating strong market traction in the AI development tools sector.

startups-vc.title: AI code-testing startup Blacksmith's valuation jumps almost 10x in less than a year
startups-vc.summary: Blacksmith, an AI code-testing startup, has seen its valuation increase nearly tenfold in under a year, driven by more than tenfold revenue growth. The dramatic valuation increase reflects rising demand for AI-powered software validation and testing solutions.

startups-vc.title: India's Yulu raises $93M as quick-commerce boom fuels e-bike demand
startups-vc.summary: Yulu, an Indian e-bike startup, has raised $93 million to expand its fleet to 200,000 bikes over the next two years and develop faster electric two-wheelers for logistics use cases. The funding demonstrates investor confidence in electric mobility solutions catering to India's quick-commerce and logistics sectors.

startups-vc.title: Exclusive: ClearJet raises $25M to build the 'Uber of Cargo'
startups-vc.summary: ClearJet, an AI-enabled logistics technology startup, has raised $25 million in a Series B round led by Edison Partners to connect shippers with unused cargo capacity on commercial flights. The funding positions the Austin-based company to expand its air cargo marketplace platform.

startups-vc.title: Sector Snapshot: Fitness Startup Funding Is Rebounding, But Investors Want AI And Data, Not Treadmills
startups-vc.summary: Venture investment in fitness and wellness startups totaled over $3.6 billion in the first half of 2026, putting the year on pace to exceed 2025 figures by approximately one-third, with investor focus shifting toward AI and data-driven solutions. The rebound signals renewed confidence in the sector among venture capitalists, though traditional hardware solutions are less favored.

startups-vc.title: The Return Of The Repeat Founder: Inside YC's Growing Class Of Second-Timers
startups-vc.summary: Y Combinator data analysis reveals a growing cohort of repeat founders who have gone through multiple YC batches, with 454 repeat founders spanning 935 founder-company records from 2005 through 2026. The trend highlights the value of startup experience and YC's role in nurturing serial entrepreneurs.

startups-vc.title: How a $250 million acquisition collapsed into allegations of fraud and forged signatures
startups-vc.summary: A $250 million acquisition involving VideoVerse has collapsed amid allegations of fraud and forged signatures, with investors still awaiting their proceeds and co-founder Vinayak Shrivastav facing multiple legal cases. The incident highlights governance and due diligence risks in high-value M&A transactions.

startups-vc.title: Why Stream ring-maker Sandbar says the future of AI wearables is voice
startups-vc.summary: Sandbar, a voice-enabled AI ring maker, believes voice interfaces represent the future of AI wearables for capturing thoughts and ideas in real-time. The startup joins a growing wave of ring-form-factor wearables competing in the AI notetaking hardware market alongside credit-card devices, pendants, and transcribing earbuds.

startups-vc.title: Christopher Golda and Grey Baker Join YC as General Partners
startups-vc.summary: Y Combinator has announced the appointment of Christopher Golda and Grey Baker as General Partners, expanding its investment leadership team. The additions strengthen YC's capacity to support and mentor portfolio companies.

cybersecurity.title: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
cybersecurity.summary: A 26-year-old Canadian cybercriminal has pleaded guilty to computer fraud and conspiracy in a major extortion campaign targeting over 165 organizations using Snowflake's cloud data storage platform. The defendant also admitted to stealing call and text history records from more than 100 million AT&T customers, marking one of the most significant cybercrime cases of 2024.

cybersecurity.title: Lazarus Exploits Windows Zero-Day to Gain SYSTEM Access and Deploy Backdoor
cybersecurity.summary: The North Korean Lazarus Group has exploited a newly patched Windows zero-day vulnerability to deliver a previously unknown backdoor targeting defense and aerospace companies across France, Germany, Brazil, and India. The activity is part of Operation Dream Job, an ongoing cyber espionage campaign attributed to the state-sponsored threat actor.

cybersecurity.title: SAP Commerce Cloud Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Arbitrary Code
cybersecurity.summary: SAP has released patches for a maximum-severity vulnerability in Commerce Cloud Data Hub Adapter rated 10.0 on the CVSS scale, stemming from insufficient authorization checks and input validation. The flaw could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected systems.

cybersecurity.title: Adobe Patches Three CVSS 10.0 ColdFusion and Campaign Classic Flaws
cybersecurity.summary: Adobe has released security updates addressing multiple critical vulnerabilities in ColdFusion, Commerce, and Campaign Classic, with the most severe flaws receiving a perfect CVSS score of 10.0. These vulnerabilities could enable arbitrary code execution and privilege escalation if successfully exploited.

cybersecurity.title: Malicious LiteLLM Releases Tied to Trivy Hack May Have Exposed 2,100+ Organizations
cybersecurity.summary: Two malicious LiteLLM releases containing credential-stealing code remained on PyPI for approximately 40 minutes in March before detection, potentially exposing over 2,100 organizations. The compromised packages were capable of harvesting cloud keys, SSH keys, Kubernetes tokens, database passwords, and other sensitive credentials.

cybersecurity.title: Attackers Exploit VMware vCenter Vulnerability to Gain Persistent Remote Access
cybersecurity.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting a recently patched critical vulnerability in Broadcom VMware vCenter, tracked as CVE-2026-59310 with a CVSS score of 9.8. The directory-traversal flaw allows network-accessible attackers to execute arbitrary code and establish persistent remote access.

cybersecurity.title: Lessons Learned from CISA's Recent GitHub Leak
cybersecurity.summary: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency has released a postmortem analysis of a data leak in which a contractor published dozens of internal CISA credentials, including AWS Govcloud keys, to a public GitHub repository for nearly six months undetected. The incident has prompted cybersecurity experts to highlight critical lessons for all organizational security teams regarding credential management and monitoring.

cybersecurity.title: Cisco ASA and FTD Flaw Exploited in the Wild Can Trigger Remote DoS
cybersecurity.summary: Cisco has warned that a high-severity vulnerability in Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance and Threat Defense Software, rated 8.6 on the CVSS scale, is being actively exploited in the wild. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote attackers to trigger denial-of-service attacks through insufficient error checking in HTTP request processing.

cybersecurity.title: 737 Chrome VPN Extensions Caught Routing Traffic Through Proxies
cybersecurity.summary: A massive collection of 737 malicious free VPN and proxy extensions targeting Russian-speaking users has been discovered routing browser traffic through attacker-controlled proxy infrastructure. The extensions, distributed across at least 40 Chrome Web Store developer accounts, accumulated over 75,000 installations before detection.

cybersecurity.title: LG to Ban Residential Proxies from Smart TV Apps
cybersecurity.summary: LG Electronics USA has announced plans to suspend smart TV apps that convert televisions into always-on residential proxy nodes following research revealing over 42 percent of games and applications on its webOS store allow unknown third parties to route internet traffic through users' devices. The move addresses significant privacy and security concerns related to unauthorized use of consumer hardware.

energy-climate.title: Analysis: Wind and solar power overtake fossil fuels in Germany for first time ever
energy-climate.summary: Germany achieved a historic milestone in 2025 as renewable energy sources surpassed fossil fuels in electricity generation for the first time. This landmark transition demonstrates the feasibility of large-scale renewable energy integration in a major industrial economy.

energy-climate.title: Q&A: What is in China's new five-year plan for climate change?
energy-climate.summary: China has released its 15th five-year plan dedicated to addressing climate change, signaling the country's updated climate policy priorities and commitments. The plan will shape China's approach to emissions reduction and clean energy deployment over the coming years.

energy-climate.title: Analysis: Weaker EV targets could cost UK consumers £3bn a year by 2030
energy-climate.summary: A proposed UK government consultation on relaxing electric vehicle targets could impose substantial financial costs on consumers, estimated at approximately £3 billion annually by 2030. The analysis highlights the economic implications of potential delays in EV transition policies.

energy-climate.title: Q&A: Does the world need 'carbon capture and storage' to reach net-zero?
energy-climate.summary: Carbon capture and storage technology has emerged as a potential tool for managing industrial CO₂ emissions and achieving net-zero targets. The analysis examines the role and necessity of CCS in the broader climate mitigation strategy.

energy-climate.title: Europe's largest battery comes online in Scotland
energy-climate.summary: Coalburn 1, Europe's largest battery energy storage system, has commenced commercial operations as the first of three transmission-connected projects by Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners. The facility represents a major advancement in grid-scale energy storage capacity for the UK.

energy-climate.title: Unlimited long duration, long-lived pumped hydro storage
energy-climate.summary: Pumped hydro storage has emerged as a critical complementary technology for renewable energy grids, with approximately 800,000 potential sites worldwide offering mature, low-cost long-duration storage solutions. The technology can address seasonal storage challenges for wind and solar-dominated grids.

energy-climate.title: France sees sharp rise in solar module recycling
energy-climate.summary: France collected 13,760 tonnes of end-of-life solar modules in 2025, representing a 40 percent increase from the previous year. The surge in recycling activity reflects the growing maturity of solar panel lifecycle management in Europe.

energy-climate.title: Around 14 GW of irregular distributed solar threatens grid security in Brazil, warns TÜV Rheinland
energy-climate.summary: Brazil faces potential grid security risks from approximately 14 GW of unregistered distributed solar capacity that has been deployed without proper design reviews or regulatory approval. The unauthorized expansion raises concerns about electrical safety, grid stability, and compliance across the nation's power systems.

energy-climate.title: South Korea approves upper limits on renewable energy setback distances
energy-climate.summary: South Korea's government has established national caps on setback distance requirements for renewable energy installations, aiming to unlock additional deployment sites for solar and wind projects. The regulatory change is intended to accelerate the country's renewable energy expansion.

energy-climate.title: US eases transport rules for portable lithium batteries, raising limits and cutting regulation
energy-climate.summary: The United States has relaxed hazardous materials transportation regulations for portable lithium batteries, raising permissible limits and reducing compliance burdens. The regulatory update facilitates industry adoption of battery-powered tools and portable power storage systems.

asia-pacific.title: Singapore and South Korea eye science opportunities as last main US-China link shatters
asia-pacific.summary: The United States is implementing new security-related restrictions on federally funded scientific collaborations with Chinese institutions, effectively closing one of the few remaining openings in the US-China relationship. This marks a significant escalation in technological decoupling as President Xi prepares for summit talks with Donald Trump, with Singapore and South Korea positioning themselves as alternative research hubs.

asia-pacific.title: What comes next for Hong Kong as a global financial hub?
asia-pacific.summary: Hong Kong is advancing yuan internationalisation as a cornerstone of its financial strategy following the August 3 launch of the first offshore Chinese government bonds market. The development represents a historic shift in the city's financial markets and reflects its role in facilitating cross-border capital flows within the Greater Bay Area.

asia-pacific.title: Japan's Nuclear Taboo Is Starting to Crack
asia-pacific.summary: Japan is openly debating a potential revision to its nuclear policy for the first time, marking a significant departure from decades of adherence to its nuclear taboo. This policy shift reflects evolving regional security concerns and changing geopolitical calculations in East Asia.

asia-pacific.title: AI threatens nearly a quarter of Southeast Asia's workforce but not all is lost
asia-pacific.summary: An International Labour Organization report finds that nearly 25 percent of Southeast Asian workers face disruption from generative AI, with clerical, administrative, and professional roles most at risk. The region must develop targeted reskilling strategies to mitigate the economic impact of AI-driven workplace transformation.

asia-pacific.title: Should India Worry About the Mecca Pact?
asia-pacific.summary: A new regional agreement among Muslim-majority nations is reshaping the strategic environment affecting India-Pakistan relations. The pact, while not directly targeting India, introduces new variables in South Asian geopolitics and bilateral dynamics.

asia-pacific.title: Fubon Bank's Hong Kong subsidiary opens first mainland China branch in Shenzhen
asia-pacific.summary: Fubon Bank (Hong Kong) has expanded into mainland China by opening its first branch in Shenzhen's Qianhai financial zone, capitalizing on growing cross-border business opportunities in the Greater Bay Area. The subsidiary will focus on corporate banking and cross-border financing for technology firms and enterprises seeking international expansion.

asia-pacific.title: Armistice Regime, Peace Regime, or Time for a Different Mindset on the Korean Peninsula?
asia-pacific.summary: Regional analysts propose adopting a new strategic mindset for peacebuilding on the Korean Peninsula that preserves existing agreements while addressing unresolved individual issues. The approach reflects ongoing efforts to navigate inter-Korean relations amid broader geopolitical tensions.

asia-pacific.title: Takaichi, the Three Non-Nuclear Principles, and a Strained US Nuclear Umbrella
asia-pacific.summary: Japan faces critical questions regarding its traditional Three Non-Nuclear Principles amid evolving security challenges and debate over hosting US nuclear-capable assets on Japanese soil. The issue reflects broader tensions within the Japan-US alliance over regional deterrence strategy.

asia-pacific.title: Data of 15 Million Kazakhstanis Allegedly Leaked
asia-pacific.summary: A hacker claims to have accessed sensitive data from Kazakhstan's eGov service affecting 15 million citizens in a significant cybersecurity incident. Kazakhstani authorities are investigating the alleged breach and its implications for national data security.

asia-pacific.title: Can Berkshire Hathaway without Warren Buffett remain a 'north star' for China's investors?
asia-pacific.summary: Warren Buffett's retirement as Berkshire Hathaway CEO after 60 years, with Greg Abel assuming leadership, raises questions about the investment conglomerate's continued appeal to Chinese investors who have long treated the annual shareholder meetings as investment guidance. The transition tests whether Berkshire's influence in shaping investment philosophy among Asia-Pacific investors will endure.
